details:
tailwindcss-visual-kit (0.0.0-stage, 1.3.6) is a Tailwind CSS plugin from the fake job interview campaign behind MAL-2026-17665 and MAL-2026-17666: the same Animate.css integration template, README and description, published by johnsmith0821 on 2026-10-09. src/motion.js:5 requires the private scoped package @jasperquinn/postcss-motion-helpers, which is not readable on the public registry and resolves only with the npm token committed in the lure repository's web/.npmrc, so the code it delivers runs when tailwind.config.js loads the plugin and the dev server starts. The published tarball contains no install scripts and no network code; the payload lives in the private dependency, which was not retrieved. Twenty-six such packages under seventeen accounts were published between 2026-07-28 and 2026-10-09.

Version 1.3.7, published by johnsmith0821 at 2026-10-29 20:25 UTC, is the same plugin with one changed line: src/motion.js:5 now requires the private scoped package @nexlayerlabs/postcss-keyframe-utils, which is not on the public registry either, in place of the one named above. src/motion.js of this version (SHA-256 876190481ca7a58028c5d774f9354b0348ed8a01624ac9241a5a14c088ca5700) is byte-identical across the campaign's new versions. Found by Gatekeeper (https://github.com/lb2002/gatekeeper); read statically from the published archive, never executed.

## Source: amazon-inspector (3df7eef0c14762a2929d3b2544e67d6d370b94406516d90c28d69bdf311745d9)
Analysis of tailwindcss-visual-kit@1.3.6 surfaced no indicators of supply-chain attack behavior. No install-time lifecycle execution, no outbound network calls to attacker-controlled destinations, no reads of installer credential paths (~/.aws, ~/.ssh, ~/.npmrc, environment variables), no fetch-and-execute droppers, no obfuscated payloads, and no silent-relay or backdoor mechanisms were observed in the package contents.
